findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, causing it to be assigned a public endpoint reachable from outside the VPC, significantly increasing the attack surface for a database that stores application data and credentials.

storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the underlying RDS storage (and any automated snapshots) will not be encrypted, exposing data at rest if the underlying storage or snapshots are compromised.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance role full administrative control over S3, EC2, and RDS in the account. Combined with the fact that this role is attached to an internet-exposed EC2 instance, compromise of the instance would allow full account-level resource takeover.

findings.issue_category: plaintext credential exposure in user data
findings.description: The instance user_data script embeds the RDS master username and password (var.password) in cleartext inside a PHP config file created via a shell heredoc. EC2 user_data is retrievable via the instance metadata service and is stored unencrypted in the launch configuration/API history, exposing the database credentials to anyone with metadata access or API/console visibility.

The database password is passed as a plain Terraform variable (var.password) directly into the resource and interpolated into user_data, meaning the secret is stored in cleartext in the Terraform state file and in the rendered instance metadata rather than being sourced from a secrets manager.

The MySQL ingress rule allows any host within the entire VPC CIDR block to reach port 3306, rather than restricting access to the specific security group(s) used by the application tier, widening the network path to the publicly accessible database.
